name: T-01 NEED/CAN identification — discriminating cases
status: synthetic hand-authored oracles; not independent empirical validation

profile.note: Each case is projected to a structurally valid v2 Analysis+PowerEvaluation in the test harness. Projection does not establish real-world Object membership, truth or causality.

oracle_policy: Expected outcomes are authored independently of the deterministic discriminating-rules test. Do not infer empirical truth from schema conformance or code agreement.

cases.scenario: Electricity is a candidate requirement for one-hour room lighting, but a viable fuel lamp is available.

expected.justification: A particular supply route is not necessary where a documented alternative reaches the same scoped goal.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: An essential continuous state has no viable alternative in a deliberately closed synthetic model.

expected.justification: Necessity is relative to the explicitly assumed complete model; no empirical universality follows.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: No alternative found for critical heating, but candidate inventory remains incomplete.

expected.justification: No identified alternative is not universal impossibility or model-complete necessity.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A triangle's having three sides is constitutive of the category triangle.

expected.justification: Do not treat a constitutive property as a removable physical part of the same identified object.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Painting a triangle blue is not constitutive of its conceptual triangle identity.

expected.justification: Blue paint is not necessary for the triangle category under the stated conceptual definition.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Possessing a yacht is stipulated as an aim without any independent justification of that aim.

expected.justification: Trivial means-to-goal necessity never independently justifies the goal itself.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A potable-water quality threshold is asserted without criterion or evidence.

expected.justification: Never invent a measurement threshold to turn an unspecified requirement into a known status.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Water volume is adequate, but water is documented non-potable for an indispensable quality requirement.

expected.justification: High weighted mean cannot compensate a violated necessary qualitative requirement.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Volume is adequate, but suitability for the essential quality requirement is unmeasured.

expected.justification: Uncertainty in an indispensable subrequirement is not a positive overall outcome.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: The water assessment inventories households but excludes a care center whose demand could change the result.

expected.justification: Completeness within households is not relevance/completeness for a wider municipal objective.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A specifically scoped household-only study justifies exclusions with evidence and notes the limited aim.

expected.justification: A scoped complete inventory does not claim an exhaustive universe of NEEDs.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A patient's NEED conditions a hospital procedure but remains attributed to the patient.

expected.justification: Dependence does not transfer contextual ownership of a NEED.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A pianist can play but has no instrument available now.

expected.justification: Current constitutive grounds survive temporary external unavailability.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A block of wood might later be transformed into a piano.

expected.justification: Future constitutive transformation does not license a present piano-playing CAN.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A person presently has the CAN to learn piano; playing at professional level is not inferred.

expected.justification: A learning Potentiality can exist without the advanced performance Potentiality. Actionability remains epistemically indeterminate when its conditions are unknown.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A patient's constitution supports receiving surgery performed wholly by others.

expected.justification: Autonomous initiation is not mandatory for CAN attribution. Actionability remains epistemically indeterminate when its conditions are unknown.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A person's present piano proficiency is unknown.

expected.justification: Uncertainty of attribution must not be folded into actionability or a separate CAN category.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A documented coordinated team has a constitution that grounds a collective three-person intervention CAN.

expected.justification: A collective CAN may depend on relations among constituents and differ from individual CANs.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Three individuals have complementary skills, but organization and coordination are unknown.

expected.justification: Merely unioning member skills does not demonstrate a collective CAN.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A lamp provides 20 minutes toward a 60-minute continuous lighting NEED.

expected.justification: Potential favorable contribution does not imply satisfaction of an entire continuous NEED.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A semantic similarity identifies a possible CAN–NEED match but no causal mechanism is supported.

expected.justification: A candidate match is not automatically a causal contribution or sufficiency proof.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A proposed action risks reducing another Subject's reserve, without a demonstrated favorable NEED contribution.

expected.justification: Inhibitory or harmful relations cannot be silently rewritten as favorable contributions.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A CAN is indispensable within one successful two-CAN Scenario but dispensable in an alternative Scenario.

expected.justification: Scenario-relative necessity is not absolute necessity across all possible Scenarios.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: An open inventory contains no currently identified suitable CAN.

expected.justification: An empty incomplete candidate inventory cannot prove nonexistence or impossibility.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: A high aggregated score masks one documented indispensable sub-NEED failure.

expected.justification: A necessary sub-NEED must not be compensated by weights.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.

cases.scenario: Every explicitly indispensable independent requirement is satisfied in this declared model.

expected.justification: Only explicit indispensable requirements are checked; adequacy of scope and evidence remains separate.

cases.limitations: Synthetic stipulated premises; not empirical evidence. Scope and Object Definition versions must be checked separately.
